title: Install-time network policy spec and acceptance criteria for private/VPC deployments
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Purpose: capture a deterministic, testable specification for the network policy surface that must be validated during initial install and during scheduled operator upgrades of Private/VPC deployments. Motivation: customers frequently report failed installs that only surface when operator image pulls, time sync, or artifact verification fail under restricted egress policies. This ticket defines the minimal connectivity matrix, validation harness, and the acceptance gates that product, engineering, and support will use to sign off an install or upgrade in environments with constrained egress or mirrors (air-gapped or proxy-mirror setups). Scope: install-time validation of DNS, NTP, package/mirror endpoints, optional KMS/OCSP endpoints, operator handshake timeout bounds, and deterministic checksum verification. Out of scope: per-customer bespoke routing or corporate firewall rules; these are covered by onboarding playbooks and Solutions Engineering.
acceptance_criteria: Install-time validation utility (netcheck) exists and runs as a preflight job that returns a machine-readable report within 90s.

Connectivity matrix defined: DNS resolution for (a) mirror host(s), (b) signed image registry, (c) KMS endpoints (if configured), (d) telemetry ingest endpoints (if enabled) documented and validated by netcheck.
NTP validation: node clock skew < 2s after NTP sync attempt; failure should produce deterministic remediation guidance in the report.

Offline/mirror mode: netcheck detects mirror-only configuration and verifies signed artifact checksums against the provided mirror; verification must pass for >= 99.9% of artifact set used in bootstrap.
Operator handshake: control-plane operator must complete its first reconciliation loop within 120s under nominal conditions; netcheck simulates operator bootstrap and reports latency and error codes.

Explicit minimal egress allowlist documented and machine-checked (list of FQDNs/IPs + ports). Documentation includes fallback proxy/mirror configuration examples and an example iptables/snippet for common corporate firewalls.

Upgrade gate: a pre-upgrade netcheck run plus a staged canary plan (2% of nodes -> 10% -> 100%) is required; automated rollback triggers if >5% of canary nodes report connectivity or checksum failures.
Telemetry and PII: netcheck supports a redaction flag so that any produced reports omit or hash customer-identifying values by default; the test harness has a separate debug mode for SEs.

Acceptance test harness: QA can reproduce a failing network-policy scenario in a CI environment using the documented mirror image set and get deterministic failing output; test steps and artifacts are captured in the ticket.
Docs and runbook: a single-run checklist and runbook for Solutions Engineering and Support exists and is linked from Console onboarding flows.

Operatorless rollback path: documented graceful rollback procedure when control-plane is partitioned from image registry; rollback must not require internet access when mirror mode is enabled and mirror artifacts are available locally.
scope_changes: Added explicit operator-handshake timing requirement after initial draft requested only connectivity checks.
Expanded acceptance criteria to include telemetry redaction and separate debug mode for SE troubleshooting per privacy/security feedback.
Added requirement for machine-readable netcheck output to enable automated gating in CI/CD (was previously only a human checklist).
Excluded per-customer firewall rule shaping; that work will be handled by Solutions Engineering as a follow-up runbook item.
Included a staged canary upgrade plan as part of the acceptance criteria following reliability SME review.
notes: Test harness: CI job namespace ci-private/netcheck and example artifacts in s3://redwood-private-test-artifacts/netcheck-2025-02
Runbook: runbooks/internal/private-install-network-preflight.md (to be published to Customer Ops)
